newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo transporters urge lower non-customs duties.
newsitem.headline: Yugo transporters urge lower non-customs duties.

text.p: Yugoslav transporters called for lower non-customs duties on Yugoslav borders and customs terminals which were pushing prices of both exports and imports up, state news agency Tanjug reported Wednesday.
"Yugoslav transporters are faced with the growing problem of high non-customs expenses," Spasoje Spasojevic of the Yugoslav Chamber of Commerce transport committee was quoted by Tanjug as saying.

The non-customs duties, including special customs inspections, parking, health services, insurance and road tolls, have grown so much that even foreign transporters are avoiding transit through Yugoslavia, Spasojevic said.

As an example, he said a transporter from Turkey would have to pay nearly 865 German marks in various duties if he took Yugoslav roads to Europe, compared to 135 marks via longer routes through Bulgaria, Romania or Hungary.
"Our neighbours are seriously considering introduction of reciprocal measures unless our border crossing, insurance and parking costs are lowered," Spasojevic said.
According to transporters, a larger freight firm would have to set aside the dinar equivalent of 10,000 German marks a month just for parking at border crossings.
